name: boxdawn-guard
description: Judges each Bash and PowerShell command, and each read of a secret file by name, before Claude runs it: deny, ask, or no decision.

api_key.title: Boxdawn API key (optional)
api_key.description: With a key, the guard fetches signed rule updates from Boxdawn at session start (the request carries the key only). Leave empty to use the fixed rules with no network connection.

keep_blocks_local.title: Keep the deny and ask record on this machine
keep_blocks_local.description: On a paid plan the guard sends its record of deny and ask decisions (tool, deny or ask, rule ids, where the target sits; never a command or a path) to Boxdawn at session start. Turn this on to keep it on this machine only.

keep_secrets_out_of_grep.title: Keep secret files out of grep -r
keep_secrets_out_of_grep.description: Adds --exclude flags to a recursive grep in Bash so it leaves secret files out. Turn this off and no flags are added; a search that starts in a credentials folder still asks.

undo.title: Snapshot the project before each command
undo.description: On unless you turn it off. Before each Bash or PowerShell command the guard saves a copy of the project's files, ignored ones such as .env too, in the plugin's data folder on this machine. Nothing is sent anywhere. Each command waits for its copy: under a second in the projects we measured, never more than about 5 seconds. Copies take disk space (632 MB for one large project we measured). `/boxdawn-guard:undo` in Claude Code shows the copies and puts one back; so do `undo list <project folder>` and `undo restore <n> <project folder>` given to bdxguard.exe in the plugin's data folder (`current`). It needs git 2.25 or later; where it cannot work the list says so. On macOS it has been run by automated tests only. Not saved: anything outside the project folder (a database server's data, cloud resources, other folders), the project's own .git folder (commits, stashes, branches), node_modules and similar folders, build output the project's own repository ignores and holds no tracked file in (target, build, dist, out, bin, obj), repositories inside the project, on Windows folders that are links, empty folders, files over 50 MB, files that cannot be saved (ones another program holds open, or with a name git does not take, such as `nul`), pipes, sockets and devices. While a pipe, a socket or a device stands under the name .gitattributes, .gitignore or .gitmodules in a folder the copy goes into, no copy is taken at all, and the list says so; a restore leaves a file as it is while one named .gitattributes stands in its folder or one above, and names it. On Linux a symbolic link comes back as the same link; on Windows links have not been checked. What comes back is each file's content, not its read-only or hidden mark, modified time, alternate data streams or hard links, and on macOS and Linux not its permissions beyond whether it can be run, its owner or its extended attributes; a file renamed only in letter case comes back under its old name. A file changed by an edit tool is saved before the next Bash or PowerShell command. At the start of a session, a project's copies older than 7 days are dropped, and its oldest ones while they take more than 2 GB; the newest always stays; at every session start, on or off, all copies of a project not used for 30 days are removed. A session opened in the home folder, a drive, or Desktop, Documents, Downloads or OneDrive itself takes none. A command that runs before its copy is ready, as in a large project at the start of a session, shows as NO SNAPSHOT in the list and is not protected. A project so large that its first copy takes over 30 minutes gets none, and the list says so. This is for an agent's mistakes, not for an agent working against it: the copies are not kept from the agent, which can read them, .env included, or spoil them with a command that reaches the plugin's data folder. A command line that names the guard's own `undo restore` asks first, and is refused where nobody is there to approve it (as in bypassPermissions mode).

undo_instead_of_git_asks.title: Let a snapshot stand in for asking about git reset --hard and the like
undo_instead_of_git_asks.description: With snapshots on, a line that is only `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- .`, `git restore .` or `git stash` in the project's own repository, and only rewrites files a snapshot holds, goes on without asking once its snapshot is taken, also where nobody is there to approve it (bypassPermissions). Anything else on the line, a doubt about which files git reaches, or a snapshot that is late or leaves a file out keeps the ask.

language.title: Language
language.description: The language of the guard's messages. Auto follows this machine's language.
